segment.description: Brush Creek (Cocke County) — a TWRA hatchery-supported trout creek in the Big Creek corridor of Cocke County (catalog). Identity verified by county: all five 'Brush Creek' rows in TWRA's 2026 stocking schedule are Cocke County (Region 4), matching the catalog's Cocke County / HUC 06010105 (French Broad) / GNIS 01278672 entry; other Tennessee Brush Creeks (e.g., a separately promoted stocked Brush Creek in Greene County) are different waters and carry no rows here.
segment.boundaries: Whole creek in Cocke County as stocked by TWRA; no formal agency reach boundaries documented.

coldSource.notes: No cold-water source documented. No dam, no spring influence, no elevation figure in any checked source. The stocking program type is the agency signal: five Seasonal-type (spring) rainbow rows (weeks of 3/8 through 5/3/2026) and no winter entries, and the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 classifies hatchery-supported streams as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. Program design is spring put-and-take: the creek's only TWRA 2026 rows are five Seasonal-type Rainbow Trout stockings (3/8, 3/22, 4/5, 4/19, 5/3/2026).

wildPopulation.detail: Not on TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list (trout regulations page checked 2026-09-18 — no Brush Creek entry; catalog concurs) and no wild trout record found in any checked agency source. Note: a native brook trout restoration project exists on Trail Fork Big Creek, a different Big Creek tributary, not on Brush Creek.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Spring-only put-and-take rainbow water: TWRA's 2026 schedule stocks Brush Creek (Cocke Co.) solely as five Seasonal March-May rainbow events, with the Trout Management Plan classifying hatchery-supported streams like this as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'.
